pencereler.0-5: An Amtrak train plunged off a bridge into an Alabama bayou. Carriages sank and
pencereler.5-12: burned, and forty seven people died. Minutes earlier, a barge had hit the bridge in thick fog. The towboat
pencereler.12-20: pilot didn't realize it was a railway bridge. The impact bent the track out of line. But the rails didn't break, so
pencereler.20-30: the signals stayed green. The train reached the kink at full speed. Towboat crews then had to be trained to use their radar.

bulgular: 12-20s: no central mystery or problem is posed

segmentler.metin: The Big Bayou Canot bridge derailed a passenger train into a bayou.
It took only a towboat lost in fog pushing a barge into the bridge.
So how could a towboat lost in fog pushing a barge into the bridge do this?

The answer is barge impact displacing a span and kinking the track without breaking the signal circuit — and it is why towboats got radar training requirements and bridges near waterways got better protection.
